audit.why: 51.49% over 402 games. Levels 1-3 are free against a melee with no gap-closer, Frenzied Maul evens 4-5, and Stormbringer plus bruiser items take the rest.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven stages are sided 'Skill'. whys[0]-[2] all describe a free Jayce poke window at levels 1-3, whys[4] says 'Volibear owns this window' at 6, and late says 'This is where you lose the straight 1v1' — yet 2+ items is sided Jayce.
audit.why: A chart that is Skill almost everywhere says nothing, and the two stages that ARE decided are decided the wrong way round. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Volibear|Skill|Volibear matches the captions.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Volibear, Skill, Volibear.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) spikes[1] calls his ultimate 'Stratospheric Push'. It is Stormbringer. (b) Four fields say the R 'shields him'. Riot: Stormbringer grants BONUS HEALTH; the shield in his kit is Sky Splitter (E), and only if Volibear himself is inside the blast radius. (c) Thundering Smash is described as a charge that lands a stun. Riot: it grants speed towards enemies, 'Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks' — the stun rides his next attack, not the cast.
audit.why: (a) is the calibration-list error class. (b) matters for the all-in maths — bonus health is not absorbed-then-gone, and knowing the shield is Sky Splitter tells you it only exists when he stands in his own E. (c) is why Thundering Blow works against his engage: knock him back before the attack lands and there is no stun at all. The page gave the correct advice without the reason.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer named, bonus health replacing 'shield', Sky Splitter's self-shield condition noted, and the stun-rides-the-attack rule stated in early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul is repeatedly called a heal with no mention of the condition or of Grievous Wounds, and its on-hit application is never noted.
audit.why: Riot: it damages and MARKS the target; casting again on the SAME target deals bonus damage and heals him. So the first Maul does not heal — breaking off after it costs him the whole payload. It also applies on-hit effects, so his damage scales with attack speed and armour alone reads the trade wrong. Both were flagged missing for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Second-cast condition stated in mid; on-hit and Grievous Wounds in late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Thundering Smash 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, Frenzied Maul 5s flat, Sky Splitter 16s flat, Stormbringer 160/135/110s. The 12s Q is the engage you hold Thundering Blow for; the 160s R at rank 1 is a genuinely long window to fight in.

edits.after: His R, Stormbringer, disables your turret, hands him bonus health, and leaps through your poke to dive — your R is just the Cannon/Hammer stance-swap, no new ult spike, so this window is his.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours: take Cannon Q and gate-Q every step-up he makes to last-hit, because a melee Volibear has to walk into your orb to farm. Drop Acceleration Gate and fire Shock Blast through it for the accelerated chunk, and hold Thundering Blow (Hammer E) to knock his Q charge straight back out before he lands the stun. Don't dump mana proving a point — he has no gap-closer up yet, so just stack a health lead off his last-hits.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours: take Cannon Q and gate-Q every step-up he makes to last-hit, because a melee Volibear has to walk into your orb to farm. Drop Acceleration Gate and fire Shock Blast through it for the accelerated chunk. Thundering Smash does not stun on cast — it stuns the first enemy he ATTACKS — so Thundering Blow knocks him out of the charge before that attack ever lands. He has no gap-closer up yet, so stack a health lead off his last-hits.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you still poke him off the wave, but his W (Frenzied Maul) heal is now closing the gap on your chip, so trade in bursts — Cannon Q, swap to Hammer for the armor/MR shred, then Q-E-W — and reset, never sit in a long brawl he wins. Level 6 is the flip: his R disables your tower, shields him, and lets him leap through your poke, while your own R is just the stance-swap you already had. Respect that all-in, save Hammer E for his Q charge, and don't get caught shoved under turret when his ult is up.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you still poke him off the wave, but Frenzied Maul is closing the gap on your chip — and note it only HEALS on the second cast against the same target, so breaking off after the first Maul costs him the payload. Trade in bursts: Cannon Q, swap to Hammer for the armor/MR shred, then Q-E-W, and reset. Level 6 is the flip: Stormbringer disables your tower, hands him bonus health, and leaps through your poke, while your own R is just the stance-swap. Save Hammer E for his 12s Q and don't get caught shoved under turret.

edits.before: This is where you lose the straight 1v1. By two items Volibear is a tanky brawler who survives your full combo, heals it back with W, and his Q stun into R leap turns any caught-out into a death — and you built zero defense. Your whole game was the early plates and health lead, so cash it into objectives and side-lane priority before he scales. Never facecheck him at 2+ items, and let your team soak the engage.
edits.after: This is where you lose the straight 1v1. By two items Volibear survives your full combo and heals it back with a second Frenzied Maul, which also applies on-hit — his damage rides attack speed, so buy Grievous Wounds, not just armour. His Q stun into an R leap turns any caught-out into a death and you built zero defense. Cash the early plates and health lead into objectives and side-lane priority before he scales.

notes: 'Stratospheric Push' is not a Volibear ability — his R is Stormbringer, and it grants bonus HEALTH, not a shield. The only shield in his kit is Sky Splitter (E), and only when he stands in his own blast. Thundering Smash's stun rides his next attack rather than the cast, which is the actual reason the page's 'knock his Q charge back out' advice works. Frenzied Maul heals only on the second cast against the same target and applies on-hit — both flagged missing for this matchup.
